title: Compass v2.0 beta
description: Work with the eight lenses and five moves in the published beta. Keep different accounts visible, choose a practical intervention, and return to what it teaches you.
introduction: Commissioning is the public craft of helping a place form and reform the relationships, capabilities, arrangements and conditions through which people can live well, with the system learning from what happens.

source.title: Compass v2.0 beta: commissioning as collective system learning
source.author: Benjamin P Taylor
source.note: The matrix wording is transcribed from the published beta. The final lens heading has been joined across a line break. Saving, perspective comparison, decisions, and review records are additional features of this online edition. No maturity score is calculated.

questions.label: Opening up
questions.prompt: What system of life are we looking at, above and below the visible service landscape?

questions.label: Sensemaking
questions.prompt: What conditions are making wellbeing easier, harder, fragile or unsustainable?

questions.label: Strategising
questions.prompt: Which conditions, if changed, would make the biggest positive difference without pretending we control the whole?

questions.label: Making change
questions.prompt: Change rules, resources, rhythms, infrastructure and relationships so living well becomes easier before crisis.

questions.label: Collective learning
questions.prompt: What have we learned about the conditions that shape whether people can live well? Which patterns are becoming clearer? What has changed in the place, not just in the service? What are we now seeing that our previous boundary hid?

sections.title: Good relations and patterns of organising

questions.label: Opening up
questions.prompt: Who is in relation, who is outside, and whose absence is treated as normal?

questions.label: Sensemaking
questions.prompt: Where is trust strong, where is conflict hidden, where do interfaces break, where does goodwill mask bad design?

questions.label: Strategising
questions.prompt: What relational infrastructure is needed: shared routines, repair, conflict work, joint learning, decision rights?

questions.label: Making change
questions.prompt: Create practical spaces where people act together around real situations, not perform partnership.

questions.label: Collective learning
questions.prompt: What have we learned about how relationships actually work under pressure? Where did trust grow, where did it break, and where did formal partnership conceal weak relation? What needs repair, renegotiation, or more honest conflict?

questions.label: Opening up
questions.prompt: Whose capability counts: residents, families, neighbours, practitioners, civic groups, local enterprises, public bodies?

questions.label: Sensemaking
questions.prompt: Where is capability growing, depleted, blocked, over-professionalised or made dependent?

questions.label: Strategising
questions.prompt: Where should capability sit closer to life and where does specialist capability genuinely matter?

questions.label: Making change
questions.prompt: Invest in edge authority, community capacity, practitioner judgement, peer support, civic infrastructure and mutual help.

questions.label: Collective learning
questions.prompt: What have we learned about whose capability increased, whose reduced, and whose was ignored? Are people, communities, practitioners and local organisations more able to act now than before? Where did our help create dependency rather than agency?

questions.label: Opening up
questions.prompt: Who defines what a good life means here? Who is named as a problem rather than recognised as a person?

questions.label: Sensemaking
questions.prompt: What do people actually ask for, in their words? What matters over time? Where is the system making outcomes worse?

questions.label: Strategising
questions.prompt: Which outcomes should be defined by people and place, and what decision rights should follow?

questions.label: Making change
questions.prompt: Change measures, governance, conversations and accountability so lived purpose shapes action.

questions.label: Collective learning
questions.prompt: What have people told us, through experience not just consultation, about whether life is better? Who still isn’t shaping the definition of success? What outcomes are being claimed by the system but not recognised by people living with the consequences?

questions.label: Opening up
questions.prompt: What counts as knowledge? What is invisible because it does not fit current categories?

questions.label: Sensemaking
questions.prompt: What patterns appear across stories, demand, cost, failure, weak signals, professional judgement and place knowledge?

questions.label: Strategising
questions.prompt: What learning questions matter most now? Which uncertainties need tests rather than reports?

questions.label: Making change
questions.prompt: Build shared sensing, rapid feedback, open evidence, learning reviews and experiments that alter practice.

questions.label: Collective learning
questions.prompt: What did the experiment or intervention teach us? What signals did we notice too late? What evidence changed our mind? What should now be made visible to others in the system, and what should stop being counted because it misleads us?

sections.title: Agency, shared action, and convening change

questions.label: Opening up
questions.prompt: Which constraints are real, which are interpretations, and which protect important rights?

questions.label: Sensemaking
questions.prompt: Where do law, policy, finance, risk and governance close down agency? Where are they being used imaginatively?

questions.label: Strategising
questions.prompt: What room can be legitimately widened, and who must share the risk?

questions.label: Making change
questions.prompt: Create permissions, safeguards, delegated authority, pooled arrangements, ethical risk practice and lawful flexibility.

questions.label: Collective learning
questions.prompt: What have we learned about real and imagined constraints? Which rules, risks, policies or governance habits turned out to be more flexible than assumed? Where do we need stronger legitimacy, safeguards, or shared risk to widen room for action?

questions.label: Opening up
questions.prompt: Who decides, who can challenge, who can stop harm, and who can call for learning?

questions.label: Sensemaking
questions.prompt: What are the actual decision rhythms? Where do choices get stuck, displaced, escalated or hidden?

questions.label: Strategising
questions.prompt: What decision architecture would fit the uncertainty and variety of the work?

questions.label: Making change
questions.prompt: Set up cadences for choosing, resourcing, testing, reviewing, adapting and stopping.

questions.label: Collective learning
questions.prompt: What have we learned about how decisions are made, delayed, displaced or avoided? Were the right people able to define, decide, resource, challenge, stop and learn? What decision rights need to move closer to the situation?

sections.title: Forms of assets help, infrastructure, and action

questions.label: Opening up
questions.prompt: What forms of help are imaginable beyond existing services and contracts?

questions.label: Sensemaking
questions.prompt: Which forms actually fit people’s situations? Which create dependency, fragmentation or avoidable work?

questions.label: Strategising
questions.prompt: What mix of forms best fits the context: grants, alliances, neighbourhood practice, contracts, mutual aid, direct support, shared infrastructure?

questions.label: Making change
questions.prompt: Test and adapt the forms. Keep the form subordinate to purpose, relationship and learning.

questions.label: Collective learning
questions.prompt: What have we learned about which forms of help fit the situation? Which contracts, grants, alliances, neighbourhood arrangements, direct support, civic infrastructure or informal forms helped? Which created friction, dependency, exclusion or avoidable work?

reviewQuestions: What changed in people’s lived experience?
What did we learn about how the system behaves?
What did we learn about our arrangements, rules, measures, relationships and forms of help?
What did this reveal about who we think we are, what we think we are here for, and whose purposes count?
